    • Funding Compendium 2025
    • Partnerships for progress

    Support to United Nations system programmes, offices and initiatives

    In 2025, UNDP continued to serve as the institutional platform for four UN entities, delivering critical services across the UN system.

    Support to United Nations organizations: UNDP continued to be the operational backbone of the UN system in 2025. It disbursed $2.3 billion in 109 currencies through its payroll system, 54 percent of which was on behalf of partner UN organizations. UNDP supported $3.2 billion in financial transactions for 70 UN entities and other agencies in 170 countries. In addition, UNDP provided common premises for other agencies in 130 countries, enabling them to access common services, including travel management.

    United Nations Volunteers

    The UN Volunteers programme promotes volunteerism to support peace and development worldwide. During 2025, 17,169 UN Volunteers from 182 countries supported 59 partner UN entities in their peace and development activities in 172 countries.

    UN Capital Development Fund

    In 2025, the UN Capital Development Fund provided $6 million in loans and $3.1 million in guarantees, leveraging and catalysing a total of $50 million in financing to support development solutions in 19 countries. Through UNCDF-enabled solutions, 3.3 million people were reached, of whom two-thirds were women.

    Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office

    The Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office transferred $1.06 billion to participating UN and non-UN entities in 2025, supporting development, climate and environment, and peace and transition outcomes for sustainable development progress. As a system-wide UN asset, the MPTF disbursed over $860 million to 41 UN entities and 111 countries in 2025.

    UN Office for South–South Cooperation

    In 2025, the UN Office for South–South Cooperation supported 41 UN resolutions and decisions that incorporated South–South and triangular cooperation modalities. It also facilitated the implementation of South–South and triangular cooperation trust fund projects across 50 developing countries.
